newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up across the board on Friday, thanks to overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active December 1996 contract ended at 20,560 yuan ($2,475) per tonne, rising 130 yuan. It opened at 20,590 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 20,630 and a low of 20,540.
September rose 100 to 21,200 yuan, October 130 to 20,880, November 120 to 20,620, the January 1997 contract 150 to 20,550 and February 190 to 20,590.
Combined volume rose to 15,615 tonnes from 5,025.
Copper opened up and moved at a high level for most of the session, with later-maturing contracts breaching the key resistance level at 20,500 yuan.
Traders said that gains on the LME gains encouraged short-covering and fresh buying to push copper up.
"Many investors expected copper to test the $1,970 resistance level on the LME, and Shanghai copper to follow it in the next few days," one trader said.
"Optimistic expectations pushed late-maturing contracts over 20,500 yuan, but it will not breach the key 21,000-yuan level on poor fundamentals and technical factors," he added.
"Long liquidation will emerge below the 21,000-yuan level, since most of the buying was speculative," a second trader said.
Aluminium ended up. September rose 40 to 14,390 yuan per tonne, October 40 to 14,300 and November 50 to 14,300.
Combined volume fell to 410 tonnes from 580.
